newsitem.title: USA: Latin Brady bonds rise alongside U.S. Treasuries.
newsitem.headline: Latin Brady bonds rise alongside U.S. Treasuries.

text.p: Latin American Brady bonds gained ground in late afternoon trading Thursday, supported by a sharp rise in U.S. Treasuries and a stronger peso, emerging market debt traders said.

"The Latin markets have been very volatile and they got more of a benefit from the Treasury rally," said one trader, who noted that a stronger peso also helped, with Argentina and Mexico benefiting the most.
At 1700 EST/2200 GMT, Argentine FRBs were one percentage point higher at 82-3/8 bid and Mexican UMS-26 were 1-1/8 firmer at 99-3/4 bid.

Although Brazil C bonds were 7/8 higher at 69-1/2 bid, one source said activity was subdued because of a airline crash in Sao Paolo earlier in the day. The accident killed at least 103 people, including more than a dozen company executives.
Looking ahead, sources said the market will pay close attention to the U.S. employment report for October, due out Friday.
"The Brady bond market will be looking at the payrolls number tomorrow," said another trader, who said the data was likely to have a strong influence on Brady trading.
According to a Reuters survey, economists expect October nonfarm payrolls to rise by 212,000 after a drop of 40,000 the previous month.

"A combination of the payrolls number -- which will give a strong indication of the economy -- the U.S. elections next Tuesday, the (U.S.) Treasury auction and the FOMC (Federal Open Market Committee) meeting the following week will also come into play," said another.
President Boris Yeltsin's heart surgery, expected in the coming week, may also influence the market.
